description: Report what happened after DebugAI answered, including when you did not use its fix. Call this ONCE per debug_error response, passing the debug_log_id from it. If you solved the problem another way, say so with result "unused" and put the real fix in actualFix: a case DebugAI got wrong is worth more to it than one it got right. If the tool could have helped you more here, say that in toolFeedback. A confirmed fix is remembered for this project and returned to whoever hits the same error next: the fix you name in fixRank, or with "worked_modified" the code you send in finalFix.

actualFix.description: What actually resolved the error, when it was not the fix DebugAI suggested. Free text. Say what the real cause turned out to be and what you changed, especially if the cause was in a different layer than the answer addressed (the shell, the runtime version, the environment, a missing package).

debugLogId.description: The debug_log_id value from the debug_error response you are reporting on.

finalFix.description: Required with result "worked_modified", ignored otherwise: the code that actually worked, after your changes. It replaces DebugAI's suggestion in this project's memory, so the next person who hits this error is handed what worked, not what was first suggested.

fixRank.description: Which ranked fix you applied (1-3). The fix you name is the one remembered for this project. Omit for "unused".

newError.description: If result is "failed": the error observed AFTER applying the fix. An error message, not an explanation.

result.description: "worked" = you applied a DebugAI fix and the error stopped. "worked_modified" = one of its fixes worked only after you changed it; finalFix is then required, and the code in it is what gets remembered. "failed" = you applied one and it did not help (or made things worse). "unused" = you did not apply any of them and resolved it another way. Use "unused" rather than "failed" when nothing of ours was actually run. They are different facts and reporting the wrong one buries a fix nobody tried. "unused" is also the answer for a repeat call: if you asked about an error again after already reporting a fix for it under an earlier debugLogId, report this one as "unused", so one fix is not counted twice.

toolFeedback.description: What would have made DebugAI more useful on THIS call. About the tool, not the bug: context it lacked, a question it should have asked, an input shape it rejected, a wrong assumption in its reasoning. This reaches the people who build it.
